claim: D/F theory has been tested almost only by coding transcripts to the box diagram. The one independent test (Pontis & Blandford 2016) fit in outline but needed new activities and cycles, and set up no prediction that could fail.
agent_test: Not testable on the agent. Use as a warning that frame labels are descriptive: measure outcomes (accuracy at equal tokens), not label fit.

claim: Reframing is rare and trigger-driven. In 44 structure tasks nobody reframed; people grew one frame by adding anchors. In pilot surprise cases, reframing came after surprise, conflict and failed explanation. Cost side (indirect): wrong LLM answers show 418% more thought switches than right ones (Wang 2025), and one model changed 98.7% of answers when asked to revise (Stav 2026). No study yet compares trigger-based and always-reframe arms.
schema_part: O (reframe fires only on a trigger)
agent_test: Count reframes per run. Compare an always-reframe-every-k-steps arm with a trigger-only arm at equal tokens.
audit_note: Minor: 98.7% is a Codenames clue revision rate for Claude Haiku 4.5 (not all answers), and the 44-task/no-reframing result is from 11 participants on structure tasks only.

claim: Experts differ from novices by questioning source quality, discarding data points and elaborating the frame longer before accepting a name. The reasoning process is shared; the knowledge base differs.
schema_part: G (do not accept the first frame fast)
agent_test: Force a minimum elaboration step (list what the frame predicts, check one prediction) before commit, versus none, at equal tokens.
audit_note: Minor: the 'shared reasoning process, different knowledge base' sentence is Rankin et al. restating Klein et al. 2007 second-hand, and Pontis is only 5 experts vs 6 novices.

claim: Frame activities are not cleanly separable or ordered. Elaborating and comparing run at once, sequences are messy, and coders had trouble separating them. Rankin et al. add abandoning the search and rapid switching.
agent_test: Do not hard-code an order of activities. Test a fixed pipeline against free choice of the next activity at equal tokens.
audit_note: Minor: Pontis says 'more than two activities occurred simultaneously' made decomposition hard (it does not mention coder disagreement stats); the evidence note b01 saying all frame activities were seen contradicts a02 (3 unobserved), but the claim does not use it.

claim: The current frame decides what is noticed. Cues that are not salient or not expected are missed, and slow changes give no surprise, so nothing triggers questioning. LLMs also keep an early wrong frame.
agent_test: Plant a slow drift in a multi-step task. Compare an agent with a per-step 'frame predicts X, observed Y' check against none.

claim: A prompted step to question the first diagnosis raised accuracy in dermatology students on easier cases (76.8% vs 60.1%, p=.004), with a smaller non-significant effect on harder cases (22.7% vs 16.7%, p=.080), and no overall change in confidence or calibration (calibration p=.19; on easier cases calibration was better in the reflection group, p=.016). In internal-medicine residents, structured reflection tended to counter an availability-bias deficit (Mamede 2010). Gap 3 note: no LLM study splits the question-first-answer gain by item difficulty; the nearest (Stav 2026) found gain unrelated to baseline accuracy (rho 0.05) and related to verifiability (rho 0.65).
agent_test: Add a question-first-answer pass; score easy and hard items separately and track calibration.
audit_note: Accuracy numbers match (76.8 vs 60.1 p=.004; 22.7 vs 16.7 p=.080), but 'no gain in calibration' holds only overall (p=.19): on easier cases the reflection group was better calibrated (p=.016); the residents availability-bias clause has no source among those listed and JAMA 2010 says reflection 'tended to counter' the bias, not removed it.
claim_before_audit: A prompted step to question the first diagnosis raised human accuracy on easier cases (76.8% vs 60.1%), with a smaller non-significant effect on hard cases (22.7% vs 16.7%) and no gain in calibration. Reflection also removed an availability-bias deficit in residents. Gap 3 note: no LLM study splits the question-first-answer gain by item difficulty; the nearest (Stav 2026) found gain unrelated to baseline accuracy (rho 0.05) and related to verifiability (rho 0.65).

claim: LLMs cannot reliably fix their own answers without an outside signal. Intrinsic self-correction did not help and often hurt (CommonSenseQA GPT-3.5 75.8 to 38.1 then 41.8; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 91.5 then 89.0). GPT-3.5 GSM8K barely moved (75.9 to 75.1 to 74.7). Gains need oracle labels (GPT-3.5 GSM8K 75.9 to 84.3). Correction: c18 wrongly says 75.9 to 95.5. Update (gap search): the 2023 picture is too strong for 2026 models. Five 2026 models gained from intrinsic self-correction on average (SAT Haiku 4.5 75.64 to 93.59), and the gain tracked verifiability (rho 0.65) not baseline accuracy (rho 0.05); still up to 13.25% of right answers turned wrong and one model rewrote 98.7% of clues. Tools beat no-tool critique in CRITIC (ChatGPT HotpotQA F1 52.9 vs 46.1 vs CoT 42.8). A model-only check on graph coloring fell to 1/100 (Stechly).
schema_part: G (a bare 'reconsider' is not verification); O (question needs an outside check)
agent_test: Compare a bare re-check, a re-check with a tool or test result, and no re-check at equal tokens. Split items by how checkable the answer is, not by difficulty. Log right-to-wrong flips.
audit_note: Minor: GPT-4 CommonSenseQA barely moved (82.0 to 79.5 to 80.0) and the 98.7% figure is Haiku 4.5's Codenames revision rate; all quoted numbers match Tables 2 and 3 of Huang et al., CRITIC, Stechly and Stav.

claim: Reflect-and-retry is task dependent. On iAgentBench it helped Claude Sonnet 4.5 (0.648 to 0.682) but slightly hurt on SimpleQA (0.740 to 0.716).
agent_test: Run reflect-retry per task type and keep it only where it pays.

claim: Models fall into a wrong group frame set up by red herrings. GPT-4 0-shot solved 6 walls (239 groups) on the original Only Connect set and 59 walls (595 groups) when red herrings were removed. Re-checked at source.
agent_test: On a distractor-heavy set, compare with and without a 'list two other groupings first' step at equal tokens.

claim: LLMs confirm more than they falsify on rule discovery. Success tracks the disconfirming-test ratio. A counter-example prompt raised discovery from 42% to 56% on average, and Think-in-Opposites helped in all 11 settings. Negative testing is the main driver in a second benchmark (reasoning models 68-75% vs instruction-tuned 33-41%). Detail: Think-in-Opposites raised success in 11 of 11 settings and Dual-Goal in 8 of 11; gains significant for thinking models, mixed for non-thinking; Blicket transfer Qwen3-32B 0.57 to 0.86. In humans the opposites step alone (not just listing properties) carries the effect: 78.33% vs 38.33% vs 36.66% (N=180). Open diagnosis: a counterfactual critique step was worth about 5 points (79.2 vs 74.0) in one troubleshooting agent, cost not reported.
agent_test: Add a 'test the opposite of your last test' rule on a debugging or diagnosis set where an opposite is defined by an assumption. Measure disconfirming ratio, success and tokens.
audit_note: Minor: FalsifyBench 68-75% are only the top two reasoning models (GPT-5-Nano 12%, Qwen3.5-9B 21%), and the SIA ablation is a single small-sample agent (100 scored cases).

claim: The falsification gain can be trained into small models and transfers to a causal Blicket task (Qwen3-8B 0.21 to 0.59 with teacher plus Think-in-Opposites). Training is outside our scope.
agent_test: Out of scope (training). Note only.

claim: Prompt-only debiasing of anchoring is weak. Chain of thought, ignore-the-anchor and reflection gave no significant gain. Showing anchors from both sides helped partly. More thinking tokens did not reduce bias (delta +0.031, p=.157).
agent_test: Compare bracket-both-sides prompting with reflection at equal tokens.
audit_note: Minor: Lou and Sun tested only GPT-4 and GPT-4o on 62 questions; Kraishan's delta +0.031 is reasoning vs sibling non-reasoning model across 4 families, and the restate-the-anchor effect (p=.057) was not significant.

claim: Premature closure is large in frontier LLMs. They pick an answer when the correct option is removed (about 70% false action at baseline, about 48% with a safety prompt) and close most on underspecified low-risk cases (73-96%). Narrative closure was also the default on ambiguous social cases (only 12.5% held ambiguity open).
agent_test: Add an explicit 'none fits: ask or abstain' path and measure false-action rate on removed-answer items.
audit_note: Minor: narrative-closure evidence is a small sample (72 responses, 24 prompts, 3 models) from a different task and population than the medical false-action results; 'default' is the authors' 87.5% not-open figure (40% narrative closure).

claim: LLMs commit early to a reading and fail to recover. Multi-turn loss averages 39% (aptitude -15%, unreliability +112%). Recaps recover only part (snowball 15-20%). In clinical information seeking wrong early frames mostly stay wrong, but recovery varies by model (Opus 4.6 7 of 8, Qwen3 Next 1 of 14).
schema_part: S (hold frame open until evidence); memory (restate all facts)
agent_test: Compare restate-all-facts and held-open-frame arms with none on staged-information tasks.
audit_note: Minor: recovery counts (7 of 8, 1 of 14) rest on very small per-model denominators in one clinical study; 'recaps recover only part' is strictly snowball (15-20%); recap on last turn did better.

claim: Whether LLM fixation on familiar patterns is a lasting weakness is contested. Older models were below physicians (best 50% vs 66% mean), while a 2026 reasoning model reached 0.751 vs physicians 0.66 on the same benchmark family. Gap search: both papers are from one group and one 100-item set (5 physicians); best model went 50% (Dec 2024) to 75.1% (2026). Generation effect is the simplest reading, but it is not independently replicated and 25% of answers on the hardest 20 items were decisively wrong.
agent_test: Re-run a fixation benchmark on our own base model before building anything for it. Build only if a gap remains.

claim: The frame-comparison technique ACH did not improve coherence or reduce bias in several studies (N=227 null, F=0.002; N=24 null; N=50 null second-hand). Layout of evidence did matter (hypotheses in rows: 39% vs 62-67% chose the confirming hypothesis, N=161). Trained analysts were mostly not biased (66% balanced, N=62).
schema_part: O (compare: do not copy the ACH matrix as is)
agent_test: Compare a matrix-style compare step with an informal one at equal tokens, and vary the layout.
audit_note: Minor: the N=50 Whitesmith figure could not be verified (second-hand, as the claim itself says); Karvetski and Mandel report ACH sometimes produced worse performance (Mandel 2018), not merely null; Lehner's N=24 null is on projection error only.

claim: Showing evidence for and against hypotheses with no recommendation (evaluative AI, built on D/F) did not beat no-AI in the first behavioural test (N=375; Brier recommendation-only 0.173, model 0.178). A rival report (Le et al. 2024a) claims a gain, unopened.
agent_test: Interface question for humans. Low priority for a single agent.

claim: The Plausibility Transition Model (Klein 2023) predicts abrupt gap closure and rising strain before reframing. No prediction was tested. It was built from 23 cases judged by one reviewer.
agent_test: Count unexplained anomalies. Trigger seek-frame when the count crosses a threshold. Compare thresholds at equal tokens.

claim: Separating facts from interpretations (Diagnosis of Thought) lifted cognitive-distortion recognition from 0.425 to 0.956, where generic chain of thought and reasoning models did not.
schema_part: O (elaborate: split data from frame inference)
agent_test: Add a data-versus-inference split inside elaborate and compare at equal tokens.

claim: Staged sensemaking structure helps, and finding the frame is the bottleneck. Pirolli-Card eight-stage trajectories gave more diverse, better outputs. On True Detective GPT-4 went from 0.38 (chain of thought) to 0.83 when given the golden reasoning.
agent_test: Compare staged against free reasoning at equal tokens on abductive tasks.

claim: The wording of a case sets how the model closes it. First-person framing changed alignment (teacher-student 4/9 vs 0/9 third person).
agent_test: Restate the problem in neutral and alternative narrations and measure answer shift.

claim: Frames come in clusters tied to a deep story. Swapping one rumour frame left the underlying story intact, so a reframe should be checked for shared assumptions.
schema_part: O (reframe: must differ in a stated assumption)
agent_test: Require a reframe to differ in at least one stated assumption and score answer diversity.

claim: A formal D/F sketch exists (extract evidence, retrieve hypothesis set, score, threshold tau, then elaborate or seek). It can be implemented directly and has no empirical test. Gap search: Klein 2023 supplies no numeric tau, strain count, anomaly tolerance or frame limit, so tau must be tuned, not copied.
agent_test: Implement the three functions as prompts and compare with plain chain of thought at equal tokens.

claim: An ACT-R model reproduces confirmation, anchoring, representativeness and probability matching from blended instance retrieval, not coded rules (R2 .645 vs 45 humans; .591 on new data).
agent_test: Check whether blended retrieval of past cases causes anchoring in our memory design.

claim: Nothing in the open sources gives numeric trigger rules for D/F. Klein 2023 defines anomalies as violated expectancies, strain as qualitative, and stopping as plausibility 'experienced as sufficient'. No tolerated anomaly count, frame limit or hypothesis limit appears. The 'up to 3 frames' figure remains second hand because the 2007 chapter and the FOCUS report could not be opened (403).
agent_test: Treat anomaly threshold, strain count and frame limit as tunable parameters. Sweep them on a misleading-first-frame set.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-26 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: A model-only check is weak and an outside signal is strong. Tool-based critique beat or matched no-tool critique in every CRITIC QA and math row (one exact tie: text-davinci-003 SVAMP, 80.7 both); a model-only check on graph coloring accepted only 2 of 100 optimal colorings, and in 39 of 40 cases where the generator had produced an optimal coloring the verifier hallucinated same-colour adjacent pairs. For 2026 models the gain from a no-tool revision correlates with verifiability (rho 0.65), not with baseline accuracy (rho 0.05).
schema_part: O (question must call a tool or test where one exists)
agent_test: Arm A: reconsider in text. Arm B: reconsider with a run or lookup. Report gain by checkability and right-to-wrong flips.
audit_note: CRITIC with tool did not beat no-tool in every row: text-davinci-003 SVAMP is a tie (80.7 vs 80.7); other QA and GSM8k/TabMWP rows do favour the tool (e.g. ChatGPT HotpotQA F1 52.9 vs 46.1).
claim_before_audit: A model-only check is weak and an outside signal is strong. Tool-based critique beat no-tool critique in every CRITIC QA and math row; a model-only check on graph coloring accepted only 2 of 100 optimal answers and invented conflicts in 39 cases. For 2026 models the gain from a no-tool revision depends on checkability (rho 0.65), not difficulty (rho 0.05).

claim: An evidence-conditioned commit gate is the only measured commit rule found. Holding edits until listed observations were made raised SWE-bench Verified pass@1 by 4.8 to 11.8 points and cut tokens 1.4% to 12.1%. Structured conditions beat the same conditions as prose (58 vs 68 solved of 100). Self-agreement across runs is not a safe stop signal because runs can agree and be wrong.
schema_part: O (commit only when expected observations are present)
agent_test: Replace 'stop when plausible' with a checklist of expected data per frame; compare with a fixed-step stop and a self-agreement stop at equal tokens.

claim: Explicit hypothesis state held in structure helps diagnosis, but writing the same procedure into the prompt did not. A controller-held belief state raised maj@3 F1 from 8.6 to 86.1 (GPT-5.1) over ReAct; ReAct told to follow the same algorithm stayed near zero. Structured evidence state beat prose state by 10 of 100 in ECLoop. No study tests an in-context frame object (anchors, expected data, open anomalies) at equal tokens.
schema_part: S (state is an editable frame object, kept by code if possible)
agent_test: Three arms at equal tokens: free text; frame object written in context; frame object held and checked by code.

claim: Agents notice conflicts early but do not keep them. Conflict mentions peak in the first 10% of a trajectory, accuracy on conflict items fell more than 30 points on TMD, and prompting for unresolved conflicts raised escalation (GPT-5 MoNaCo 1.6 to 60.7) while lowering accuracy (30.1 to 23.2).
schema_part: S (open-anomaly list persists) and a cost test on surfacing
agent_test: Log anomalies in a list that survives context; test whether resolving or parking them changes the answer.

claim: The seven Chinn and Brewer responses (ignore, reject, exclude, abeyance, reinterpret, peripheral change, theory change) give a finer operator list than preserve versus reframe, and they set two data factors (credibility, ambiguity) that predict whether theory change happens. The original was not opened, and no LLM study uses the list.
schema_part: O (anomaly handling beyond preserve/reframe: park, discount source, patch, reframe)
agent_test: Label what the agent does with an anomaly using the seven classes; test whether adding park and patch operators beats a two-operator set.

claim: Whether reframes that differ in a stated assumption beat rewordings is untested. Only a way to score the difference exists: compare what hypotheses predict (GEAR beta, mean pairwise Jaccard dissimilarity). Diversity and accuracy rose together in GEAR training, and a bigger hypothesis set is not better by itself (ToT held 21 and scored lowest).
agent_test: Generate reframes in two arms (assumption-changing vs reworded). Score prediction dissimilarity and final accuracy.

claim: The experts' extra steps (source checks, discarding data, longer elaboration) have no accuracy test in the sources found. Gap 10 stays open. The only related LLM facts are that agents drop conflicts they noticed and that surfacing conflicts can cost accuracy.
schema_part: G (do not accept the first frame fast): keep as a test, not a rule
agent_test: Ablate each expert step alone on a labelled set and compare accuracy at equal tokens.
